python.title: Decorators and context managers
python.lead: Phase 02 lesson: Decorators and context managers. Cross-cutting behavior and safe cleanup.
keyPoints: Cross-cutting behavior and safe cleanup
A decorator wraps a callable; a context manager brackets a block. Preserve metadata and guarantee cleanup on both success and exceptions.

sections: Explain and apply Decorators and context managers in a realistic workflow.
A decorator wraps a callable; a context manager brackets a block. Preserve metadata and guarantee cleanup on both success and exceptions.

Separate retry policy from the operation: retry only transient failures, cap attempts, use a delay/backoff policy where appropriate, and never retry validation or authorization failures blindly. excel.lead: Phase 02 lesson: Data Tables, Goal Seek and Scenario Manager. Sensitivity analysis with explicit assumptions.
keyPoints: Sensitivity analysis with explicit assumptions
Goal Seek changes one input to reach one target. A one- or two-variable Data Table substitutes input combinations into a formula; Scenario Manager stores named assumption sets.

sections: Explain and apply Data Tables, Goal Seek and Scenario Manager in a realistic workflow.
Goal Seek changes one input to reach one target. A one- or two-variable Data Table substitutes input combinations into a formula; Scenario Manager stores named assumption sets.

Model: Profit = (Price-Cost)*Units
Goal Seek: target Profit cell; changing Price cell
Two-variable table: row inputs = price; column inputs = units

A Data Table is a sensitivity tool, not a forecast: results only reflect the model and assumptions supplied. Confirm the row/column input cells are the intended model inputs, the output formula references both, and calculation settings permit recalculation. Scenario Manager stores values, so document assumptions and do not mistake scenario names for probability estimates.

powerbi.lead: Phase 02 lesson: Relationships: cardinality, filter direction, bridges, role-playing dates. Make filter propagation intentional.
keyPoints: Make filter propagation intentional

Use dimension-to-fact one-to-many relationships with single-direction filtering as a default. Use bridge tables for many-to-many mappings; activate an inactive date relationship in a measure when needed.

sections: Explain and apply Relationships: cardinality, filter direction, bridges, role-playing dates in a realistic workflow.

Use dimension-to-fact one-to-many relationships with single-direction filtering as a default. Use bridge tables for many-to-many mappings; activate an inactive date relationship in a measure when needed.

Orders[OrderDateKey] -> DimDate[DateKey] active
Orders[ShipDateKey] -> DimDate[DateKey] inactive
Shipped Sales = CALCULATE([Net Sales], USERELATIONSHIP(Orders[ShipDateKey], DimDate[DateKey]))

powerbi.lead: Phase 02 lesson: DAX: CALCULATE, FILTER and time intelligence. Understand measure evaluation in filter context.
powerbi.highlight: Understand measure evaluation in filter context
keyPoints: Understand measure evaluation in filter context

CALCULATE evaluates an expression in modified filter context; FILTER returns a filtered table. Use a complete date table for classic time intelligence and test selected periods and fiscal/calendar assumptions.
Connect this concept to the phase project and verify it with a small independent test.
sections: Explain and apply DAX: CALCULATE, FILTER and time intelligence in a realistic workflow.
Understand measure evaluation in filter context

CALCULATE evaluates an expression in modified filter context; FILTER returns a filtered table. Use a complete date table for classic time intelligence and test selected periods and fiscal/calendar assumptions.

Net Sales = SUM(FactSales[NetSales])
Large Sales = CALCULATE([Net Sales], FILTER(FactSales, FactSales[NetSales] > 1000))
Sales YTD = TOTALYTD([Net Sales], DimDate[Date])
Sales LY = CALCULATE([Net Sales], SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR(DimDate[Date]))

CALCULATE modifies filter context, so explain each filter argument in business terms and test a measure under multiple slicer selections. FILTER over a large fact table may be less efficient than a simple Boolean filter argument when the condition permits it. Ensure the date table is complete and covers all selected periods; document calendar versus fiscal year and handle periods with no transactions.

powerbi.title: Excel Phase 3 prerequisite: Power Query and data modeling
powerbi.lead: Prepare the same sales dataset and modeling concepts in Excel before building the Power BI semantic model.
powerbi.highlight: Power BI Phase 02 assumes familiarity with Excel Phase 03 Power Query transformations and data-modeling basics; complete that Excel phase first, as specified in the course sequence.
keyPoints: Excel Phase 03 is a prerequisite bridge, not an additional Power BI topic.
Practice Power Query merge, append, unpivot, group by, Applied Steps and basic M concepts in Excel.
Understand query folding and parameters at a conceptual level, then identify facts, dimensions and relationship keys.
Use consistent field names and business definitions when moving the prepared dataset into Power BI.
sections: Confirm readiness for Power BI Phase 02 by completing the Excel Phase 03 preparation and documenting the resulting dataset and model assumptions.

In Excel, import the sales source, inspect column types and nulls, standardize keys, and use Power Query to perform repeatable transformations. Distinguish merge (join columns from related tables) from append (stack rows with compatible schemas). Unpivot cross-tabbed period columns into a normalized row structure when the analysis requires a date/period field.

Name steps by intent, keep source and transformation stages distinct, and avoid unnecessary repeated conversions. Parameters can centralize file paths or date limits. Query folding means compatible transformations may be translated and executed by the source; whether a step folds depends on connector and operation, so verify rather than assume.

Declare the fact grain; list candidate dimension tables and unique keys; identify date roles such as order date and ship date; check for duplicate dimension keys and orphan fact keys. Preserve raw source data separately from cleaned outputs so transformations can be audited.

Treat the hand-off as a reproducible data contract: record source files, transformation steps, column types, key rules and expected row counts. Reconcile totals before and after Power Query, then verify Power BI relationships do not multiply rows. Accept the dashboard only when measures reconcile at total and sliced levels and the report's date role is explicit.
syntaxNotes: Merge joins tables horizontally using matching keys; append stacks rows vertically and requires compatible column meaning.
Converts multiple attribute columns into attribute-value rows, often making time-period data easier to model.
A Power Query optimization in which transformations are delegated to the source when supported; inspect the query plan/indicator for the actual connector and steps.
A precise sentence defining what one row in the fact dataset represents.
powerbi.code:
Excel Power Query hand-off checklist:
1. Confirm data types and key uniqueness.
2. Merge lookup attributes by stable keys.
3. Append only schema-compatible period extracts.
4. Unpivot period columns when periods are represented as separate fields.
5. Record transformations and verify row counts before/after.
powerbi.practice: Complete the Excel Phase 03 Power Query and Power Pivot lessons first. Then prepare a sales dataset and hand-off package: clean tables, data dictionary, grain statement, relationship-key checks, and a reconciliation of source versus transformed row counts. Bring that exact package into Power BI Phase 02. Submission evidence: include the finished artifact, a short explanation of the design choice, and test evidence for at least one normal case and two edge cases.

knowledgeCheck.question: What is the key difference between merge and append?
knowledgeCheck.answer: Merge joins related columns by key; append stacks compatible rows from one table beneath another.
